name: Updating Two-Dimensional List (Case 2)
description: Construct a program that initializes a 3x3 two-dimensional matrix that has the numbers 1 through 9 for entries, updates the middle row to a list filled with 1s, then sets the top-right element of the matrix to be 10, and finally prints the matrix.
code:
#Step 1: Define a 3x3 two-dimensional list 
matrix = [[ 1, 2, 3 ],
          [ 4, 5, 6 ],
          [ 7, 8, 9 ]]
#Step 2: Update the two-dimensional list 
matrix[1] = [1, 1, 1]
matrix[0][2] = 10
#Step 3: Print the list
print(matrix)

commentList: We need to use two-dimensional list (a list of lists) to create a matrix. Each matrix row corresponds to a sublist in the two-dimensional list. This statement creates a 3x3 two-dimensional list called matrix and initializes its entries with numbers 1 through 9.
Note that lists can naturally span multiple lines if we want them to because they are contained by a pair of brackets.
This statement assigns a list of 1s to the middle row of the matrix.

In a two-dimensional list, we can get an entire matrix row (a nested sublist) by using one index. The row index could start at 0 and continue up to but not including the length of the two-dimensional list, i.e., the number of rows in the two-dimensional list matrix.

In this statement, the list on the right-hand side of the assignment operator is the new list that we want to assign to the matrix row. The index of the middle row in the matrix is 1. So, matrix[1] corresponds to the middle row in the matrix.
This statement sets the top-right element of the matrix to be 10.

In a two-dimensional list, we can access an element within a matrix row (a nested sublist) by using two indices. The first index in [] is the row index and the second index in [] is the column index. The row index could start at 0 and continue up to but not including the length of the two-dimensional list, i.e., the number of rows in the two-dimensional list. The column index could start at 0 and continue up to but not including the length of the row, i.e., the number of elements within the row.
The top-right element of the matrix has the row index of 0 and the column index of 2. So, matrix[0][2] corresponds to the top-right element of the matrix.

We can see the content of the two-dimensional list by calling the print function and passing the two-dimensional list to that. This statement will print the entire matrix followed by the end-of-line character.
